messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC: proposing we split the grace period into three independent slices (warm, drain, settle) instead of one monolithic TTL. Reason: different safety/availability tradeoffs per phase and easier observability

devon: I like the split. Can you sketch the invariants for each slice? e.g., what operations are allowed in warm vs drain vs settle.

maya: Sure — rough sketch: 
- warm (0-30s): requests routed to old and new region in parallel for reads; writes prefer old region. Used for fast traffic shadowing.
- drain (30s-3m): stop routing new sessions to old region; allow in-flight tokens to finish. Writes still go to old region if residency_required, otherwise routed to new with a write-redirect header.
- settle (3m-15m): slow background reconciliation, KV lease handoff, and final cutover. After settle we decommission old lease.

aj: That seems reasonable. Two quick questions: 1) who enforces the 30s/3m/15m numbers? 2) how do we handle long-lived sessions (mobile idle clients)?

maya: 1) Defaults enforced by region-proxy with per-tenant overrides in the tenant manifest. 2) long-lived sessions get a special flag `session_pin` that extends drain/settle or triggers manual review. We don't auto-extend forever.

ria: Product note: some enterprise customers will require a hard residency guarantee, meaning writes must fail in non-resident regions during all phases. Can we model that as `residency_required=true` in the routing policy?

devon: Yes — routing policy supports `residency_required` and `preferred_region`. If residency_required and we don't have resident capacity, we return 409 + structured hint for client-side retry or queue. Avoid silent fallback.

maya: Example config we discussed in the RFC: 
```
grace_windows:
  warm: 30s
  drain: 3m
  settle: 15m
soft_cutover:
  max_inflight: 10
  prefer_local: true
  residency_required: false
```

aj: Operational concerns: automatic cutover will need good signals. I suggest we gate transitions on 3 metrics over a rolling window: p50 request latency, error rate increase, and in-flight sessions count. If any of these are outside thresholds, we pause and extend current slice.

devon: +1. Also add `recent_kv_conflicts` and `write_retries > X` as safety signals. Reconcilers should emit events to ops channel when we auto-extend.

maya: Agreed. Proposal for thresholds (default): p50 < 200ms, error_rate_delta < 0.5%, in-flight < 100 per shard, kv_conflicts < 0.1%

ria: From compliance POV we need an auditable trace of the cutover timeline and per-tenant overrides. That means every state transition must be persisted to the control plane and snapshottable. Also a small UI to manually force/abort transitions.

maya: Noted — control plane will store a compact state machine log per tenant. We'll surface an action audit (who pressed pause, who forced cutover).

oncall-bot: Incident hint: if grace_phase is extended > 30m for > 10 tenants in a region within 1h, raise SEV-3 and alert oncall.

aj: UX for client SDKs: expose `CutoverHint` header with values `preferred_region`, `residency_required`, `cutover_phase`. That will help SDKs decide whether to hold or retry.

devon: Implementation note: runtime needs to be able to evaluate per-request routing policy cheaply. Plan: compile tenant manifest into a small routing trie cached at proxies. Updates are pushed via incremental delta.

maya: Outstanding open questions I want folks to weigh in on: 
1) default slice durations (are 30s/3m/15m sane?)
2) should we allow per-model overrides (some models are more stateful and may need longer settle)?
3) metrics & dashboards to monitor (what exact dashboards do SREs want?)

aj: For SREs: dashboard per-region with phase counts, pct migrated, replication lag (kv apply lag), and per-tenant recent conflict rate. Also a global cutover health page.

ria: Product: per-model override is useful. Would like an escape hatch: `fast-path=true` for low-risk models for which customers can opt-in to a reduced settle window.

devon: My only pushback: too many knobs will become unwieldy. I recommend 2 layers: global defaults + per-tenant overrides. Avoid per-model unless requested by customer support flow.

maya: Good point. We'll expose per-tenant and per-service tuning for now. If customers ask for per-model we can add later.

aj: I'll add alert playbook drafts (auto-extend, manual rollback, emergency abort) and drop in the runbook doc.

maya: Thanks — I'll update the RFC text with the slices, config schema, and the control-plane audit requirement. Ping me with any other concerns. :sparkles:
